coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Parcel K South (PKS)
record.summary: The southern piece of the Port's 20th/Illinois Street parcel, on Illinois Street south of the new 21st Street, reserved under the 2017 approvals as a 100%-affordable housing site (65 ft under the D4D). The Port's 2026 report assigns it to Phase 2 and says its gap funding is not yet available; no developer has been selected.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward). It is Parcel K South, a Port-retained parcel created from the Port's Illinois & 20th Street Parcel (Port Item 9B, Res 17-52), outside the 28-Acre Site and the developer's vertical option, so it is not within Brookfield's 28-acre district. It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer shows the surrounding Pier 70 land re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address), and Port Item 9B gives the Illinois & 20th Street Parcel as Block 4110 Lot 001 (DataSF lists 4110001 as retired 2018-10-02). RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (how the shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository, https://github.com/pierandpoint/record) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. This deliberately does NOT match today's satellite imagery of the parking lot -- this parcel's boundary represents the D4D's planned footprint, including '21ST ST (NEW)', which is not built yet.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. PKS is part of the Port's Illinois & 20th Street Parcel (Assessor's Block 4110/Lot 001 per Port Item 9B), which Resolution 17-52 has the Port subdivide into four parcels; it is outside Brookfield's 28-acre site, so the earlier statement that it is part of that site is withdrawn. DataSF lists 4110001 as retired (2018-10-02); which current lot corresponds to PKS has not been checked, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential in every D4D land-use scenario (Figures 1.5.5-1.5.7), 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2, and a 100%-affordable housing site under Port Item 9B. A real parcel distinct from Parcel K North: Port Resolution 17-52 (Item 9B, Sept 2017) has the Port subdivide the 20th/Illinois parcel into four parcels including Parcel K North and Parcel K South, and the Port's Item 12B memo (Feb 2020) names 'the Illinois/20th Street parcels known as Parcel K North and Parcel K South' (its Resolution 20-07 recital says 'the Illinois/20th Street parcel known as Parcel K', singular). No source found gives a specific unit count, architect, or construction-status beyond this.

facts.value: 100% affordable housing (one of three stand-alone affordable parcels with C1B and C2A)
Port of San Francisco (Port-controlled parcel outside the developer's option)
no more than six residential stories (D4D S6.4.2)
Phase 2 (affordable) / Phase 2B in Exhibit A, with C1 (Port's 2026 report)

The 2017 Affordable Housing Plan requires at least 30% of units at the 28-Acre Site and Parcel K South be affordable, including 320 or more permanently affordable units in three buildings developed by local nonprofits; the 2026 proposal keeps a 327-unit stand-alone minimum while lowering the project-wide rate to no less than 20%

The D4D lets the Retail and Service frontage for HDY3 and HDY1/2 be combined on 22nd Street; Irish Hill Corner Plaza sits at the corner of Illinois and 22nd Streets between HDY3 and HDY1/2 (D4D Section 3.11), not at PKS

changes.text: The 2033 completion milestone is now labelled a soft 2017 outside date that down market delay has tolled and Port Item 11A proposes to reset, not a current expectation. Resolution 17-52 is described as the Parcel K North sale approval that subdivides the whole 20th/Illinois parcel, and the DDA is said to cover Parcel K South's horizontal improvements but not its vertical option.
